speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces; to determine the cause, please tell me if you have a fever, fatigue, or a rash elsewhere on your body. Also, have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes or joint pain recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your new captopril use and symptoms of oral/genital ulcers alongside forearm blisters, I need to rule out a severe drug reaction; have you experienced difficulty breathing, a widespread rash, or swelling of your lips/tongue? Also, regarding your recent hiking trip, did you have any insect bites or specific plant exposures other than poison ivy?

speaker: Patient
text: includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: SJS/TEN (Stevens-Johnson Syndrome/Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis) secondary to captopril.

*Note: The diagnosis is based on the classic triad of cutaneous blisters, mucosal ulcers, and the timing of initiation of a known culprit drug (captopril). Immediate discontinuation of the medication and supportive care are required.*
